title: Costa Mesa officer pleaded guilty after personal Flock tracking
summary: The Orange County District Attorney said former Costa Mesa officer Robert Jay Josett used Flock and other confidential police databases to locate his wife, an ex-girlfriend, and another person. He pleaded guilty to three misdemeanor counts and received three years of informal probation.

sources.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases
key_claims: The DA said Josett used Flock to track his wife, ex-girlfriend, and another person.
The DA said he continued accessing Flock after being placed on leave.

statutes_or_policies: Unauthorized computer access and fraud
Contempt of court
Annoying and repeated phone calls

outcomes: Josett pleaded guilty to three misdemeanor counts.
He was sentenced to three years of informal probation.

review.notes: The source is a verbatim syndication of the Orange County DA release.

title: Orange City officer accused of repeated Flock tracking
summary: A Volusia County arrest affidavit, as reported by WKMG, said Orange City officer Jarmarus Brown repeatedly searched three vehicles in Flock over roughly seven months while allegedly stalking a former partner. Brown was arrested, and a later Florida certification report recorded his no- contest plea to a computer offense.

The report said Brown was arrested on stalking and improper-computer-access charges.

sources.title: Criminal Justice Standards and Training Commission Spring 2026 Quarterly Update
key_claims: The state report records Brown's no-contest plea to a computer offense and a certification sanction.

statutes_or_policies: Stalking
Unauthorized access to an electronic device

outcomes: Brown was arrested.
Florida's certification report recorded a no-contest plea and a 60-day suspension followed by one year of probation and ethics training.

review.notes: Claims about searches are attributed to the arrest affidavit as reported by WKMG.

title: Norfolk residents challenged warrantless citywide Flock tracking
summary: Two Norfolk-area residents sued the City of Norfolk and its police chief, alleging that the city's network of more than 170 Flock cameras creates a searchable record of drivers' movements without a warrant or probable cause in violation of the Fourth Amendment. The complaint was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

sources.title: Complaint for Declaratory and Injunctive Relief, Schmidt v. City of Norfolk
sources.publisher: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia
key_claims: The complaint alleges Norfolk's Flock network records drivers' movements without warrants or probable cause.
The plaintiffs sought declaratory and injunctive relief under the Fourth Amendment.

statutes_or_policies: Fourth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution

outcomes: The federal complaint was filed on October 21, 2024.
The litigation challenged continued warrantless collection and searching of Flock data.

review.notes: The record describes filed allegations and does not state that liability was established.

The plaintiffs sought declaratory and injunctive relief under the Fourth Amendment.

statutes_or_policies: Fourth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution

outcomes: The federal class-action complaint was filed on April 15, 2026.
Plaintiffs requested limits on retention and warrantless access plus nominal damages.

review.notes: The record describes filed allegations and does not state that liability was established.

title: Milwaukee officer sentenced after repeated personal Flock searches

The reports say he later pleaded guilty to attempted misconduct in public office, resigned, and received probation and a fine.

key_claims: A criminal complaint said Ayala used authorized database access 179 times for personal reasons.
